text: Hmmmm . . . I've been repeating this song and still trying to decipher it. And ever since the teaser, i can't expect anything from their debut song. But i kinda wanted to know the message behind this MV, coz it's like a mix of 3 things. Introduction, statement and finale~ The intro are on a spectacular scale, it's like BOMB-drop with a super strong hip-hop'ish music style that i can find on SWF performances. ( but the girls said it's still only a teaser ) And then the 1st switch, it's like watching ITZY's debut colors and then fall back further to TWICE prime era with the bright concept and fun. They ended with a strong rock-ish melody and saying "eottae-yo" which means how was it? By that lyrics i feel like JYPe message are : This is NMIXX , an ALL-ROUNDER. They can do any concept, any challenge. The binoculars choreo part means "watch us carefully". At least that's how far i could decipher the message of this debut song. I might sound too much sugar coating, yes it sounds weird , it really does sounds like 3 songs mixed into 1 just like some netizens said here. But to me , i think i will go with 'ICONIC'. Either beyond someones expectations or below. Either a hit or a miss. One thing for sure, there is confidence on it. Coming both from SQU4D and from the girls NMIXX themselves. Oh right , this MV also contain one of the most intriguing ending scene which somehow giving me a sad feeling. That's right , when Jiwoo stares on the 'faint doughnut' lamp sign . . . I still don't know what that means but i kinda have an idea , as one group have a song with that title. Anyway, congratz girls on your debut! Your 1st page of NMIXX!! Let's MIXX this world!!!

author: @starhoshibyul
text: You might not believe it but I was there back then.. When Twice also got hates on their debut song, when people actually called LOA messy too. People called it flops which was understandable, it took long time for it to naturally climb up the chart from the bottom seriously. They also never win any music show with their debut song ok. Even Cheer Up -- which made them popular nationally, & TT -- which made them famous overseas, also got called like a messy mash up of different songs too. When Itzy debuted most people dislike Dalla Dalla, calling it messy and was like wth but then come back few days later and say they like it.. SKZ got called out for their noisy, measy music. They only got their first win after several comeback. It was only recently that they finally charted in Melon -- with an album that they named what haters called them: "NOEASY". And if you look at their album sell growth, it's like one of the most organic growth of sales you will ever see, despite them coming from JYP where ppl say they hv the Big 3 privilege. Thing is I know fans nowadays all care about breaking records and all (sadly for some it's for bragging rights first, & the groups are like their 2nd priorities) but this is only the beginning of a journey so let them follow their own pace. Like JYP once said to SKZ (before they ever win any music show) -- It's even more meaningful if people stay because they find what they like about you, instead of jumping into the hype. Anyway sorry for the rants. I just feel like some people need to realise this.

author: @dripfanmo
text: NMIXX - O.O (6.5/10) As usual, people are being so nitpicky (and harsh) to a newly debuted JYP girl group, knowing that every JYP gg always rises on top. I understand the criticisms, the song is confusing and there is no "strong hook" to compensate for the mixtures. As a lyricist, wala ring essence ang meaning unlike other gg debut songs from JYPe. Thus, for me, it is their first extreme experimental song. I have expected a lot. Pero knowing this kind of mix genre concept, it is a GROWER. Personally, I would have chosen Tank (and make the arrangement more strikey) than this. But it's too early to judge O.O, let some days pass. Gano'n din naman nangyari sa Dalla Dalla ng ITZY dati, it received massive amount of dislikes before but later on people loved it and it became the biggest gg hit in 2019 and biggest gg debut hit on 4th generation. JYPe marketed the group as a "vocal" group, I wish they should have stayed there and focused on highly vocal technique-powered songs and less on experimental approaches. Nonetheless, congrats NMIXX ! 👏

author: @missl9702
text: This is a very confusing and hella risky debut song honestly. I dont like it at first listen, even in my second time. It was on my fourth try listening in the song when I somewhat got to digest it. On my fourth try of listening to the song I realize this song is like a roller-coaster ride! This debut song is a loud music that not everyone will appreciate but dont get me wrong, I like loud music as to what mostly people prefer calling an edm sound with a slightly mix of hiphop or rock. The intro was actually good but when they start singing I didn’t expect a loud music coming in fot the first verse then the next part in which I assume was a pre-chorus part when the sound starts to relax I was like ok this part shows more of their vocal strength but then another loud banging kind of sound came which I assume was the chorus part since their choreo in that part was very strong but I honestly dont like the sound of that part. Then a pause came and another genre was shown I like this part better, this part shows their vocals clearer. Then a loud sound came again which I assume the build up part till the bridge came this is another genre once again that is a mix of edm & hiphop with a very little mix of funkiness in it that leaves me feeling a little retro with more hiphop and I like that killing part where the blonde girl (sorry don’t know her name yet) was in the center and the choreo was also nice. Nevertheless, I like the vocals and visuals of the Nmixx girls, JYP never fails to give us a top-tier girl group, but I honestly prefer “TANK” song as their debut song but I kinda understand coz that song kinda makes me remind of itzy thus I guess to give of a different flavor that this girls could offer they gave us a female version of Stray Kids but with still a different level. As for the MV it gives of the JYP quality of MVs it was like a mix of Twice, Skz, Itzy in one MV all together. Congrats Nmixx, I am actually happy to see Lily M in this group, I thought she’ll be going solo but I think she goes well with a girl group and her vocals is really amazing was mesmerize after all those years of waiting. The next thing I’ll do is to memorize all the members. The once that stand out for me the most in this MV is Lily, that blonde girl, the visual I guess coz she looks like Tzuyu and the girl that I assume as the main dancer since she’s really good in dancing she also kinda remind me of that one girl from Kep1er I forgot her name though.

author: @dovalflavia
text: (This is not a hate letter to the girls, none of this is their fault and they definitely deserve better) I went through the comments and it made me laugh how most people thought the song/mv was confusing and messy. And they're right, it is. What confuses me tho is that people have to listen to it multiple until they like it??? I've heard this statement many times before and that's the problem with 4th gen, the songs are bad, downright bad, and ppl gotta listen to it again and again until it drills into their brain and they start "liking it", which don't even sound right to me, you don't genuinely like the song, you just get used to it imo. If I don't like a song on the first listen, i won't magically like it on the second, or the third, i'll just get acostumed to it but it'll still suck. It shouldn't be confusing, or messy, or "i'll listen to it until i like it", it's music, it's not rocket science. This song is literally two songs lazily meshed together into one, which is hilarious, why couldn't they just pick one? What's so hard about it? The two different beats are good, SEPARATELY, but they ruined both with this mess. And the lyrics are probably the worst I've ever heard, what's the point of making (kinda) good music if what they're saying is just noises and empty, repetitive sentences that don't really mean anything? It screams lazy to me. I guess that's why 4th gen MVs are always so pretty and bright, something's oughta distract the viewer from the god awful music and make them think they genuinely like it... It's sad tbh, because the girls are obviously talented and beautiful, they could pull off anything, but nothing and no one can ever make this disaster sound good. I'm hoping they'll have a better comeback later on, they deserve to be successful. Wishing them the best (and better music to put their great voices to good use.)

Even the lyrics were criticized and the song was labeled “empty”. But now, it’s legendary and is considered one of the greatest songs ever made. You may not recognize it yet, but NMIXX has taken their first step towards becoming legends.
